header.name: Optical Fiber Networks for Industry 4.0
header.description: In this course, students will be familiar with Optical transport network architecture for supporting heterogenious applications of Industry 4.0 (envisioned 5G application) as per the International Telecom Union standards that drive technology towards commercialization. Further, they will get a good exposure to optimally allocate spectral resources in 5G datacenter optical networks to protect it during failures. Finally students will learn about Fronthaul technology to enable 5G slicing for low latency CloudRan and other 5G applications. This course will provide students with in-depth knowledge about network components and systems; including optical switches, multiplexers and intelligent optical amplifiers. Students will be trained on state-of-the-art simulation tools and Machine learning based physical layer noise models to calculate the signal quality of an optical lightpath.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can explain the working principle of various optical network components and systems, e.g., Couplers, Switches, Reconfigurable Add-Drop Multiplexers, ML-assited Programmable Amplfiers etc.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze the key concepts of the Coherent Optical receivers and Noise models for lightpath OSNR estimation, BER classifications.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can design Optimum Backhaul network for heterogenious application oriented Industry 4.0 with optimum allocation of spectrum and power resources.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Evolution of Optical Backhaul to FrontHaul and Midhaul while considering the key performance parameters (latency, dense deployment and jitter) to provide isolated network slicing in optical transport network for Industry 4.0 applications.
